newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korean infiltrator captured in South Korea - TV.
newsitem.headline: N.Korean infiltrator captured in South Korea - TV.

text.p: A North Korean infiltrator, one of about 10 believed to have slipped ashore in South Korea from a submarine on Wednesday, has been captured after a massive air-and-sea search, television news reported.
Munhwa Broadcasting Corporation gave no further details. A defence ministry spokesman could not confirm the report.

The search had been underway since the early hours of Wednesday morning. Troops and police had fanned out across the countryside near a beach where the infiltrators landed on the east coast close to the border with North Korea.

Earlier, Yonhap news agency said two men armed with rifles and believed to be members of the infiltration squad attacked a villager on the outskirts of the city of Kangnung before heading into nearby hills.
Yonhap quoted Kim Chang-soo, 35, as saying the men battered him with an aluminium bar. It said there had been other sightings of strangers in military uniform.
Authorities said footprints on the beach suggested about 10 people had come ashore.
